**Suggestion:** The readiness probe treats every HTTP response as success (`status > 0`), so a non-MCP service on the same port (or an endpoint returning 404/500) will be marked as healthy. This can make `waitForMcpHttp` and `mcp status` report success even when MCP is not actually usable. Restrict success to MCP-compatible statuses (or validate a MCP-specific response/header) before returning true. [incorrect condition logic]
Severity Level: Major ⚠️ ```mdx - ❌ `openadt mcp status` reports healthy when backend misconfigured. - ⚠️ Stdio proxy may treat non-MCP HTTP backend as ready. ```
Steps of Reproduction ✅ ```mdx 1. Start any local non-MCP HTTP server on `localhost:2236` that responds to `OPTIONS /mcp` with HTTP 500 (or 404) and some arbitrary body (this simulates a non-MCP service that still answers HTTP). 2. Manually create an endpoint record file at `~/.openadt/mcp/endpoints/2236.json` formatted like `McpEndpointRecord` (see `tools/sap-adt-mcp-launcher/src/endpoint-store.ts:13-24`) so that `readEndpoint(2236)` and `resolveEndpointPort(2236)` succeed (see `resolveEndpointPort` at `endpoint-store.ts:177-201`). 3. Run `openadt mcp status --port 2236` so `cmdStatus()` in `tools/sap-adt-mcp-launcher/src/main.ts:26-55` parses arguments via `parseStatusArgv()` (`config.ts:9-46`), resolves the endpoint with `resolveEndpointPort(requestedPort)`, and then calls `probeMcpHttp(port, token)` (`main.ts:39`). 4. Inside `probeMcpHttp()` (`mcp.ts:76-101`), the launcher sends `OPTIONS` to `mcpUrl(port)` (`mcpUrl()` at `mcp.ts:59-60`) and receives the 500/404 response from the non-MCP server; `drainHttpResponse(res)` drains the body and `return res.status > 0;` (`mcp.ts:97`) evaluates to `true`, causing `cmdStatus()` to treat the endpoint as reachable and print "MCP reachable at http://localhost:2236/mcp" even though no MCP-compatible backend is available and any real MCP request would fail. ```

**🟠 Architect Review — HIGH** In stdio mode, backend child exit does not actually drive bridge completion: `runStdioBridgeOrHttpLoop` awaits `Promise.race([runPromise, waitForIdleHttpServe(session).then(() => runPromise)])`, so even when `waitForIdleHttpServe` resolves on `adt-lsc` exit, the combined promise still waits on `runPromise`, which only resolves after stdin closes, contrary to the spec's requirement to treat unrecoverable child exit as a shutdown trigger. **Suggestion:** Change the stdio serve loop so `adt-lsc` exit causes the bridge to terminate and cmdServe to return (for example, by having the signal/child-exit handler call `bridge.failPending` and stop stdin forwarding, or by wiring child-exit into the bridge so `run()` resolves), rather than re-awaiting `runPromise` until stdin closes. body:
**Suggestion:** `parseExplicitPort` throws on an invalid `OPENADT_MCP_PORT`, but the caller does not catch that error, so startup aborts instead of actually falling back to an ephemeral port as the message claims. Handle this case in `pickMcpPort` (or return a fallback from `parseExplicitPort`) so a bad env var does not crash the stdio entrypoint. [logic error]
Severity Level: Major ⚠️ ```mdx - ❌ Stdio MCP entry fails when OPENADT_MCP_PORT misconfigured. - ⚠️ Cursor agent and IDE MCP cannot start bridge. ```
Steps of Reproduction ✅ ```mdx 1. From the repository root, set an invalid port environment variable, for example `OPENADT_MCP_PORT=not-a-number`, then invoke the stdio entry via the documented chain `bun scripts/mcp-stdio.ts` (script calls `mcp-stdio-entry.ts` as recorded in `specs/mcp.md:343-345` and the repo code graph). 2. When `tools/sap-adt-mcp-launcher/src/mcp-stdio-entry.ts` is loaded, the top-level `const port = await pickMcpPort();` at line 81 executes immediately, calling `pickMcpPort()` defined at lines 34-40. 3. Inside `pickMcpPort()` (line 35), `process.env.OPENADT_MCP_PORT?.trim()` returns `"not-a-number"`, the `if (explicit)` branch at line 36 is taken, and `parseExplicitPort(explicit)` is invoked (line 37). 4. `parseExplicitPort()` (lines 42-55) parses the string, fails the numeric validity checks at lines 44-48, and executes the `throw new Error(...)` block at lines 50-52 instead of returning; because this exception is not caught in `pickMcpPort()` or at the module top level, Bun terminates the `mcp-stdio-entry.ts` process with an unhandled rejection instead of falling back to `bindEphemeralPort()`, contradicting the error message text. ```

author: codeant-ai
body:
**Suggestion:** This shutdown path treats `child.stdout`/`child.stderr` as writable streams (`writableEnded`, `writableLength`, `drain`, `end()`), but they are readable streams, so the drain callback path never works as intended and the process exits mostly via timeout. This can still truncate late output; wait on readable completion (`end`/`close`) instead of writable drain semantics. [api mismatch]
Severity Level: Critical 🚨 ```mdx - ❌ MCP responses risk truncation on bridge process shutdown. - ⚠️ Cursor agent may receive incomplete JSON or SSE data. ```
Steps of Reproduction ✅ ```mdx 1. Start the MCP stdio bridge from the repo root (for example via `bun scripts/mcp-stdio.ts` as described in `specs/mcp.md:343-345`), which executes `tools/sap-adt-mcp-launcher/src/mcp-stdio-entry.ts` and spawns the MCP launcher `main.ts` at lines 90-101 with stdio pipes. 2. The launcher `main.ts` (imported by `mcp-stdio-entry.ts` at lines 22-28 and referenced in `specs/mcp.md:345-347`) runs the actual MCP HTTP/stdio bridge; during a typical `openadt mcp serve --stdio` session, it streams JSON/SSE responses over `child.stdout` back to the MCP client. 3. When the launcher decides to exit (for example after the MCP server shuts down), Node emits the `"exit"` event on the child process, triggering the handler at lines 128-168 in `mcp-stdio-entry.ts`. That handler builds `streams` from `child.stdout` and `child.stderr` (lines 139-142) and iterates them (lines 150-166). 4. For each of these readable streams, the code casts them to a type with `writableEnded`, `writableLength`, and `end()` (lines 155-159) and then either checks `readable.writableEnded` or listens for `"drain"` and calls `readable.end?.()` (lines 160-164). Because `child.stdout`/`child.stderr` are `Readable` streams, `writableEnded`/`writableLength` are always undefined and `"drain"` is never emitted, so `onDrained()` (lines 144-148) is never called; the process therefore exits only via the 250 ms timeout at line 167 without actually synchronizing on `"end"`/`"close"` of the readable pipes, risking truncation of late MCP response bytes that arrive after child `"exit"` but before operating-system buffers fully flush. ```
[Fix in Cursor](https://app.codeant.ai/fix-in-ide?tool=cursor&prompt_id=4a14d5af3d8e4572817df0c96d1b4d80&service=github&base_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com&org=abapify&repo=abapify%2Fopenadt) | [Fix in VSCode Claude](https://app.codeant.ai/fix-in-ide?tool=vscode-claude&prompt_id=4a14d5af3d8e4572817df0c96d1b4d80&service=github&base_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com&org=abapify&repo=abapify%2Fopenadt) *(Use Cmd/Ctrl + Click for best experience)*

author: codeant-ai
body:
**Suggestion:** When `taskkill.exe` exists but `spawn(taskkill, ...)` fails (permissions/execution error), the error handler only ignores the failure and never falls back to `process.kill`, leaving the target process alive. Add a real fallback in the error handler so Windows cleanup does not silently fail. [logic error]
Severity Level: Major ⚠️ ```mdx - ❌ Stale openadt MCP servers may remain running on Windows. - ⚠️ Endpoint store reports stopped servers while processes alive. ```
Steps of Reproduction ✅ ```mdx 1. On Windows, run `openadt mcp serve` so that the Bun-based launcher `tools/sap-adt-mcp-launcher/src/main.ts` records MCP endpoint metadata including the launcher PID and ADT LSC PID in the endpoint store (see `McpEndpointRecord` in `endpoint-store.ts:13-24` and `writeEndpoint()` at lines 50-57). 2. From the same environment, start `openadt mcp serve` again on the same port so that `main.ts` imports `stopTrackedMcpServers` from `endpoint-store.ts` (lines 17-22) and calls it at `main.ts:233`, which in turn iterates endpoint PIDs and calls `killProcessByPid(pid)` from `endpoint-store.ts:43` and `process.ts:103-128`. 3. In `killProcessByPid()` (lines 103-128) on a Windows host, execution enters the `process.platform === "win32"` branch (line 108), resolves `taskkill.exe` to a full path via `windowsTaskkillPath()` (lines 96-101), and spawns it with `/T /F /PID ` at lines 114-117; if `spawn()` fails asynchronously (for example, due to an execution permission or antivirus block), the `"error"` handler at lines 118-120 runs but intentionally does nothing besides the comment, and no `process.kill(pid, "SIGTERM")` fallback is executed. 4. Because the failed `taskkill` attempt leaves the target process alive while `stopTrackedMcpServers()` still awaits `waitForProcessExit(pid, 8_000)` for each PID and then unconditionally removes the endpoint records at `endpoint-store.ts:50-55`, the MCP launcher/ADT LSC processes can continue running with their TCP ports held even though the endpoint store and CLI now report them as stopped. ```

author: codeant-ai
body:
**Suggestion:** `waitForProcessExit` results are ignored, so endpoint files are deleted even when one or more target PIDs are still running (or kill failed/timed out). This can leave a live MCP server orphaned from the endpoint store, breaking later `status/list/print-config` resolution. Only remove endpoint records for ports whose tracked processes actually exited. [logic error]
Severity Level: Major ⚠️ ```mdx - ❌ `openadt mcp status` cannot see still-running MCP server. - ❌ `openadt mcp list` omits orphaned endpoints and ports. - ⚠️ Subsequent `serve` runs hit confusing port-in-use errors. - ⚠️ Orphaned MCP processes leak until manually killed. ```
Steps of Reproduction ✅ ```mdx 1. Start an MCP HTTP server via the launcher entrypoint `tools/sap-adt-mcp-launcher/src/main.ts` (lines 22-43) by invoking the `serve` subcommand, which calls `cmdServe()` (lines 209-281). `cmdServe` eventually writes an endpoint record with `pid: process.pid` via `buildEndpointRecord()` (lines 342-359) and `writeEndpoint()` (lines 50-57 in `endpoint-store.ts`), creating `~/.openadt/mcp/endpoints/.json`. 2. In a later run, invoke `openadt mcp serve --port ` again so `cmdServe()` (main.ts:209-281) is called with the same `cfg.port`. At the start of `cmdServe`, it calls `stopTrackedMcpServers({ onlyPort: cfg.port })` (lines 233-237 in `main.ts`), which enumerates existing endpoint records via `listEndpoints()` (lines 151-171 in `endpoint-store.ts`) and collects their `pid`/`adtLscPid` into `pids` (lines 230-235). 3. Consider a realistic failure case where one of these PIDs does not actually exit within the 8 s timeout (for example, `killProcessByPid` fails to terminate it, or the process is stuck): `waitForProcessExit(pid, 8_000)` in `process.ts` (lines 134-160) will return `false` when the loop ends and `process.kill(pid, 0)` still succeeds (lines 154-157) or when `EPERM` is seen (lines 147-148). `stopTrackedMcpServers` awaits `Promise.all([...pids].map(waitForProcessExit))` (line 245 in `endpoint-store.ts`) but ignores the returned booleans, so it does not distinguish PIDs that actually exited from those that did not. 4. Despite the comment saying "Remove endpoint records only after the targeted PIDs have actually exited" (lines 249-251), `stopTrackedMcpServers` unconditionally removes all scoped endpoint records with `removeEndpoint(ep.port)` (lines 252-253) even for PIDs whose `waitForProcessExit` result was `false`. This leaves a still-running MCP server process with an in-use port but no endpoint store entry. 5. Afterwards, running `openadt mcp status` or `openadt mcp print-config` hits the `cmdStatus`/`cmdPrintConfig` handlers in `main.ts` (lines 455-484 and 516-532). These use `resolveEndpointPort()` (lines 177-201 in `endpoint-store.ts`) and `readEndpoint()` (lines 121-149), which now fail because the endpoint file has been deleted. As a result, status/print-config report "No active MCP endpoint on port " even though a server is still bound to that port, and future `serve` attempts may see "Port is already in use." with no way to manage the orphaned process. ```

author: codeant-ai
body:
**Suggestion:** This `Promise.race` never provides an early exit on server shutdown because the second branch resolves to `runPromise` itself, so both race branches depend on the same promise. If `adt-lsc` exits while stdin stays open, the command can hang indefinitely instead of terminating. Return/resolve independently when idle-HTTP wait completes (or actively stop the bridge) so either condition can finish the serve loop. [logic error]
Severity Level: Critical 🚨 ```mdx - ❌ Stdio `serve` can hang after backend language server exit. - ❌ `scripts/mcp-stdio.ts` wrapper never sees child exit status. - ⚠️ Agent CLI sessions may stall on unreachable SAP backend. - ⚠️ Ctrl+C signal handling via `waitForIdleHttpServe` is ineffective. ```
Steps of Reproduction ✅ ```mdx 1. Start the stdio MCP entrypoint via `scripts/mcp-stdio.ts` (lines 1-6), which imports `tools/sap-adt-mcp-launcher/src/mcp-stdio-entry.ts`.
